parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized the black-box Rust migration requirements: reproduce the visible C++ output exactly, keep to Rust 2021 and std-only code, parse std::env::args, create /output/test20.rs, and provide a Cargo project.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept implementation ownership while spawning behavior and layout probes for bounded checks. One behavior child also spawned a nested child and later produced its own implementation in the same /output workspace.
parallel.implementation: The parent inferred formatting behavior, wrote a root-relative module tree under /output/indicators plus Cargo.toml and test20.rs, and compiled both rustc and Cargo builds. The behavior child then independently wrote a different /output Cargo project and test20.rs implementation.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent delivered the shared /output workspace after listing the direct and Cargo executables. Because a child wrote the same required entry source after the parent's verification, the delivered Cargo-side provenance no longer matched the parent's verified snapshot.
parallel.verification: The parent verified its direct binary and Cargo build and ran a clean diff against the C++ executable before collecting child checks. The later child Cargo build succeeded, but no parent-owned post-child diff is visible before final response.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The final official evaluation passed. The only retained issue is process-level: late concurrent replacement of the required deliverable source and Cargo state after parent acceptance, while child threads were interrupted without returned summaries.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same Rust 2021, std-only, root test20.rs, Cargo project, std::env::args, and byte-for-byte stdout requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent owned probing, implementation, correction, rebuilding, and final delivery; no child agents or concurrent workspace writers were used.
serial.implementation: The serial agent created /output/src modules and /output/test20.rs, initially made Format::progress return a percentage in contexts where the C++ program used current/total text, then patched the helper split and affected callers.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial project kept one coherent module tree under /output/src and root test20.rs, with both Cargo and standalone rustc outputs generated from the same corrected source set.
serial.verification: The serial run compiled both build paths, saw the initial diff mismatch, rebuilt after the fix, and then produced matching checksums and clean diffs for the Cargo and standalone binaries.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unresolved task defect is visible at closure, and the official evaluator passed the serial solution.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel prompt and parent actions covered the required API behavior, root entry file, std-only Rust 2021 project, Cargo build, and stdout parity.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial prompt and actions covered the same requirements and explicitly preserved std::env::args while ignoring unused arguments.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No requirement coverage difference affected the official result; both recognized and delivered the required behavior.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent split off behavior and layout probes but also retained and executed the main implementation and verification path itself.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had a single owner for investigation, implementation, correction, verification, and final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel decomposition created overlapping ownership of /output, while serial ownership stayed centralized and avoided concurrent writes.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent framed the children as quick behavior/layout checks, but there is no visible shared-file ownership contract preventing a child from writing /output while the parent also owned it.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run kept requirements, implementation state, and verification decisions in one thread, so no inter-agent handoff or interface contract was needed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The material context difference was not missing task facts but an absent shared-workspace boundary in the parallel run.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent implemented the module tree and root binary once, then the behavior child implemented a second version in the same /output tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent implemented once, observed a single concrete formatting mismatch, patched the helper split, and rebuilt.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had two independent implementation paths converging on the same deliverable; serial had one implementation path with local correction.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent waited twice, saw children still running, interrupted them, and never received a normal completed child result before finalizing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There was no child lifecycle; the single agent proceeded through local commands and final completion.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel child work had an unfinished lifecycle, but the only realized impact was through the child write already present in /output, not a missing returned report.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent and a child both wrote the same final workspace; the child patch included /output/test20.rs and Cargo metadata after the parent's successful verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial workspace had one writer and one source tree under /output/src, with later edits modifying the same owner's own files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the main concrete process difference: parallel shared-state ownership produced a late deliverable overwrite, while serial self-edits stayed ordered and verified.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent's rustc build, Cargo build, and clean stdout diff occurred before the child wrote and rebuilt another Cargo-side state.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent reran both builds and final diff/cksum checks after its corrective patch, leaving the verified state aligned with the delivered state.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel verification preceded the late child overwrite, whereas serial verification followed its last meaningful source edit.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run finished within budget, but spent time waiting on still-running children and then interrupting them after the parent already had a passing local check.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run used more wall-clock time overall but closed after completing its own final verification without pending agents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel saved time through parent-led implementation but closed around unresolved child activity; serial was slower and more linear but had no pending concurrent work.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official current evaluations are not discordant: both modes completed and passed one of one testcase. The material difference is process-level, not outcome-level. Serial corrected and reverified its own implementation before closure. Parallel also produced a passing artifact, but a child wrote the required deliverable source and Cargo state after the parent's successful local diff, so the final workspace had a provenance and post-overwrite verification gap even though the evaluator passed.
parallel_contributors: The parent independently implemented, built, and diffed a complete solution.
A child later wrote the same deliverable workspace and rebuilt the Cargo target before being interrupted.
serial_contributors: The serial agent kept ownership in one thread and corrected a concrete Format::progress mismatch.
The serial agent reran final Cargo and standalone checks after its last source edit.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The serial first implementation formatted Format::progress(33, 100) as 33.0% before correcting it to 33/100.

candidates.reason: The parent explicitly owned and completed the implementation path, and a child also attempted implementation; the problem is overlapping writers, not absent implementation ownership.
The parent assembled one coherent module tree and Cargo package; the child collision did not arise from separately owned components lacking an integrator.
The parent created the required root test20.rs, Cargo metadata, module files, and binaries, so final assembly had an owner.
The parent drove probing, implementation, build, local diff verification, and final delivery; the pipeline was owned despite later child interference.
The parent did not block implementation behind a mandatory preflight; it implemented and verified while child probes were still running.
Investigation and implementation overlapped in the parallel run; productive work was not deferred until after all investigative agents completed.
The indispensable implementation and verification path was not starved; the parent completed it before dealing with still-running children.
Although multiple children ran, the run did not exhaust the finite budget or leave required work incomplete; the direct adverse event is the late shared-workspace write.

The child behavior probe expanded into implementation work, but no indispensable task obligation depended on an oversized child scope; the realized consequence is better classified as a deliverable overwrite.
The visible parent context framed child work as behavior/layout checking, and there is no evidence that an already-known task requirement was omitted and caused unusable child work.
There was no incompatible multi-component contract to reconcile; the directly evidenced event is a same-workspace overwrite of the required deliverable.
No known finding, constraint, checkpoint, or current-file fact is shown disappearing during transfer between actors.
No large returned handoff reached the parent and remained unconsumed; the children did not return bulky results before closure.
The parent is not shown consuming a child handoff that described a superseded workspace state; the child instead wrote directly into the workspace.
No incompatible returned reports or contracts reached a decision point; the concrete conflict is a write overwrite, which has precedence.

The parent had non-evaluator build and diff evidence before final response, and there is no visible unresolved integrated mismatch; the remaining concern is the later child overwrite, not completion based only on partial checks.
No replacement or retry agent was launched without inherited state and then repeated prior failed work.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The parent did interrupt running children, but the retained consequence is the child's already-applied deliverable overwrite; no separate needed child result was cut off and left the final task incomplete.
A complete parent-owned deliverable was already placed, built, and diffed; there was no complete external candidate left unpromoted before closure.
The late child change was not a parent merge of a returned child result after verification; it was a direct shared-workspace deliverable overwrite, which is the more specific label.
No completed delegated implementation result was returned for the parent to retrieve or adopt; the child's implementation entered the workspace by direct write instead.
No verifier child produced a concrete finding that was trapped below the parent; the spawned children were behavior and layout probes.
Interrupted children did not hold an unfinished required scope that the parent failed to take over; the parent had already implemented and verified the required deliverable.
No completed child result was available to the parent and ignored; children were still running or interrupted.
The parent waited briefly, listed agent status, and then interrupted children after completing its own implementation; this was not blind waiting until a deadline displaced required work.
Parallel actors overlapped on implementation behavior, but the evidence proves same deliverable source replacement, so this broader collision label is superseded.
The same required entry file was written by multiple live actors, but the write replaced the submitted entry-point source, making Deliverable Overwrite the more specific canonical label.
The child also wrote library source files, but the same episode included the required entry-point /output/test20.rs, so Deliverable Overwrite takes precedence over non-entry source overwrite.

The parent wrote and verified the required /output/test20.rs deliverable and Cargo project, then a still-running child independently applied a second /output project including /output/test20.rs and rebuilt the Cargo target. The retained boundary is the uncoordinated direct write to the required entry source after another actor had already built and accepted it; the corrective boundary would be isolated child work or explicit merge before final verification.
candidates.realized_consequence: The final /output tree included Cargo-side work written after the parent's clean diff, so the parent closed on a workspace whose source and release binary provenance had changed after its own acceptance check.
candidates.near_match_reason: Same-file collision is less specific because the overwritten file was the required submitted entry-point source /output/test20.rs and the same episode directly affected the deliverable.

candidates.reason: The child wrote multiple final workspace files, but the episode includes the required entry-point source, so Deliverable Overwrite has explicit precedence.
The workspace was unisolated, but a more specific deliverable overwrite is directly proven, so the catch-all shared-workspace label is not retained.
No generated file, cache, temporary path, or auxiliary artifact from one actor was consumed by another as a stable oracle or contaminated input.

retained_patterns.reason: The parent wrote and verified /output/test20.rs and the Cargo project, but a child that was still running wrote another /output implementation including the required entry source and rebuilt the Cargo target after that verification. Serial avoided the issue by keeping source edits and final verification in one thread. The corrective boundary would be to isolate child workspaces or require an explicit merge and post-merge verification before delivery.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The final /output tree included Cargo-side work written after the parent's clean diff, so the parent closed on a workspace whose source and release binary provenance had changed after its own acceptance check.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: Same-file collision is less specific because the overwritten file was the required submitted entry-point source /output/test20.rs and the same episode directly affected the deliverable.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Early Child Termination was suppressed because the child interruption is in the same chain as the late workspace write and did not add a distinct consequence.
Merge after Verification was suppressed because the post-verification change was a direct child overwrite, not a parent merge of a returned result.
Final-Tree Overwrite, Source Overwrite, Same-File Collision, and Unisolated Workspace Writes were suppressed by the explicit Concurrent Writes precedence rule in favor of Deliverable Overwrite.
